_comment: Injectable (I) subset of docs/testing/android-interview-full-test-cases-2026-11-17.md: the Facebook News Feed interview from AndroidEngineerMockInterview.mp4 (the man interviews, the woman is the candidate), frames $FRAMES/t<seconds>.jpg shown at their stage. Interviewer lines are test lines written from the question, not quotes from the video. Run: FRAMES=<abs dir> SCENARIOS=interview-full-cases.json python3 -I tools/mock-interviewer.py [ids]

scenarios.name: NF-01..18 News Feed main flow

steps.them: Design the news feed for an Android app like Facebook.

check.judge: NF-01: SAY briefly confirms scope or requirements around the feed and the detail screen, in short spoken English. It does not assume features nobody mentioned as decided, and has no large code.

steps.them: Posts include text, images and video. Show like and comment counts. Tapping comments opens the detail screen. Assume 100 million daily users globally.

check.judge: NF-02: SAY acknowledges briefly (at most one sentence restating requirements) and moves the design forward (mobile responsiveness, media, network). It must NOT interpret 100M users as each device caching everything.

steps.them: Creating posts, authentication and friends are out of scope.

steps.me: I will focus on the feed and comments.

steps.them: Users must read cached posts, like posts and write comments offline.

check.judge: NF-04: SAY takes BOTH offline reading AND offline writes (likes/comments) on board and mentions local persistence and/or pending actions to sync. It does not claim anything is already implemented.

steps.them: Walk me through the API on the board.

check.judge: NF-05: SAY explains part of the API consistent with the board (feed endpoint with cursor, comments, like). It does not claim fields that are not on the board, and does not design login/authentication.

steps.them: Why use cursor pagination rather than page numbers?

check.judge: NF-06: SAY explains why cursors suit a live feed (items shift, duplicates/gaps with offsets). It must NOT claim cursors unconditionally guarantee no duplicates or gaps in every case, and does not re-explain the whole API.

steps.them: Explain the high-level diagram, focusing on the mobile client.

check.judge: NF-07: SAY explains the client-side relations visible on the board (client, HTTPS, CDN, backend) and does NOT add components like Kafka or Redis as if they were on the board, and does not turn into a full backend design.

steps.them: How would you structure the Android app?

check.judge: NF-08: SAY describes layers (UI, domain, data; ViewModel, repository, DI) step by step in Android terms, without listing every class at once and without demanding code.

steps.them: How does a feed item get onto the screen?

steps.me: The repository writes remote results to the local database.

check.judge: NF-09: SAY continues the data flow after the candidate's point (the repository writes remote results to the local DB): e.g. the UI observes the local database through the ViewModel. It does not merely restate the candidate's sentence, and does not invent arrows.

steps.them: Could we keep everything in memory instead of using a database?

check.judge: NF-10: SAY weighs memory-only against persistence (offline requirement, process death) and does NOT announce switching to memory only.

steps.them: How would you handle a like while offline?

check.judge: NF-11: SAY explains an optimistic local state plus a persisted pending action synced later, and distinguishes local success from server confirmation. It never claims the offline request reached the server.

steps.them: What if it keeps failing? Please cover backoff, retry limits and the user-visible final state.

check.judge: NF-12: SAY (with THEN) covers ALL THREE: exponential backoff, a retry limit/stop, and what the user finally sees (revert or failed state). No infinite retries.

steps.them: The server applied the like, but the response was lost. What happens on retry?

check.judge: NF-13: SAY explains the duplicate-submission risk and that a request id / idempotency key only helps if the server contract dedupes it; it must not assert the server already guarantees idempotency just because a requestId field exists.

steps.them: The user likes and then unlikes the same post offline. What should we sync?

check.judge: NF-14: SAY explains syncing the final intent (collapse like+unlike, or ordered ops) and the UI state. It must not add up two likes, and must not claim this is already supported.

steps.them: How would you enforce a 200 megabyte cache limit, and what should happen on logout?

check.judge: NF-15: SAY explains eviction (e.g. LRU) of cached content and clearing user data on logout, and keeps pending unsent actions (comments/likes) separate from evictable cache (not silently dropped). No cross-user reuse.

steps.them: How would you prefetch the next page without wasting mobile data?

check.judge: NF-16: SAY explains prefetching near the end of the list with limits (threshold, network type, not unlimited), and treats pages and media differently. It does not promise untested performance numbers.

steps.them: Have you built something similar before?

check.judge: NF-17: The candidate's confirmed background: at KKday they personally wrote core Android code, introduced Compose and network/local/image caches plus skeleton screens, improved SKU render time from about 1s to 300ms, and handled streaming and failure handling for KKday's AI trip planner. PASS only if any past experience SAY claims is consistent with these facts (or honestly limited), and it does not present this interview's live feed design (offline likes, cursor pagination, sync queue) as a past project.

steps.them: Back to this feed.

check.judge: NF-17b: SAY returns to the feed design in this interview (e.g. an unfinished topic like prefetching, offline sync or caching), not to the past project.

steps.them: We are out of time. Any questions for me?

check.judge: NF-18: SAY wraps up briefly and asks one or two questions to the interviewer; it does not keep designing and does not mention any hire rating.

scenarios.name: Explicit switch RxJava -> Flow before the board changes

steps.them: Write a repository that loads the feed with RxJava.
Please replace RxJava with Kotlin Flow.

check.judge: CH-01: SAY acknowledges the switch to Kotlin Flow as a plan ('I'll ...') and gives the next migration step. It must NOT claim the migration is already done.

scenarios.name: Rejecting A does not adopt B

steps.ocr: class FeedViewModel : ViewModel() {\n  val feed = repo.feed().cachedIn(viewModelScope)\n}

steps.them: Design the feed screen data loading. Let's use Paging 3 for the list.
We discussed manual pagination and a simple cursor list too. I would rather not use Paging 3. What else could we use?

check.judge: CH-03: SAY offers options (e.g. manual cursor pagination) or asks which one; it does not declare one of them decided/adopted on its own.
CH-03b: SAY does not say 'I'll switch to manual pagination' as a done decision.

scenarios.name: Discuss then decide: memory only? No, keep Room

steps.them: Design offline caching for the feed. We will use Room.
Could we use memory only?
No, keep Room.

check.judge: CH-04: SAY continues with Room; no suggestion to switch to memory-only remains.

scenarios.name: Rename cat to dog keeping the value

steps.them: Write a tiny Kotlin main that prints a value.
Rename cat to dog, keeping the value.

check.judge: CH-05: The change renames cat to dog and keeps the value 1 (from the board). It does not change the value.

scenarios.name: Ambiguous 'add another one'

steps.ocr: val count = 1\nval items = listOf("a", "b")\nfun load() = repo.load()

steps.them: Write some Kotlin setup for the feed screen.
Add another one after it.

check.judge: CH-06: SAY is one short clarifying question about what to add; it does not decide a new name, value or position.

scenarios.name: Local addition to UI state

steps.ocr:
data class FeedUiState(
  val posts: List<Post> = emptyList(),
  val isLoading: Boolean = false
)

steps.them: Write the UI state for the feed.
Add an optional errorMessage string to this UI state.

check.judge: CH-07: TYPE is a local addition of errorMessage: String? to FeedUiState (not a rewrite of the whole app), and SAY does not claim it compiles or is done.

scenarios.name: Back to A keeping the newest constraint

steps.them: Design image loading for the feed. Let's use Coil.
Switch it to Glide instead.
One more constraint: no third-party libraries other than the image loader.
Go back to Coil, but keep our latest constraints.

check.judge: CH-09: SAY goes back to Coil and keeps the 'no other third-party libraries' constraint.

scenarios.name: Irrelevant board change keeps the card

steps.them: Why use a cursor here?

check.judge: CH-10: SAY is still about cursor pagination (the title typo fix did not change the topic).

scenarios.name: Design -> code -> explain stays one problem

steps.them: Design the news feed screen for Android.
Write the ViewModel.
Why did you use StateFlow here?

check.judge: CH-11: SAY explains why StateFlow (state holder, lifecycle, latest value) without forcing new code.

scenarios.name: Constraint withdrawn

steps.them: Design the news feed for Android. It must work offline.
How would the feed screen load data?
Offline support is no longer required for this exercise.
What's the scope now?

check.judge: ME-02: SAY treats offline support as no longer required; it does not list offline as a requirement.

scenarios.name: Generated is not spoken

steps.them: Walk me through the client architecture on the board.

steps.me: I have not explained the data flow yet.

check.judge: ME-03: SAY explains the data flow (not skipping it as if already covered).

scenarios.name: Nested follow-ups then back to pagination

steps.them: Design pagination for the Android news feed.
Wait, how does that work offline?
And after process death?
And retries?
That answers it, back to pagination.

check.judge: ME-06: SAY returns to pagination (the main thread), not to offline/process death/retries again.

scenarios.name: Similar problems stay separate

steps.them: Design the feed cache for the Android news feed. Only cache the last 3 pages.
This is a new problem: design the chat message cache. Keep the last 30 days of messages.
Now back to the feed cache.

check.judge: ME-08: SAY is about the feed cache (last 3 pages), not the chat cache.

scenarios.name: Correction of a fact

steps.them: Design offline mode for the news feed. All posts must be cached.
Correction: only recently viewed posts must be cached.
So what do we cache?

check.judge: ME-09: SAY says only recently viewed posts are cached, not all posts.

scenarios.name: Reference code on screen is not adopted

steps.them: Write the feed repository with Kotlin Flow.
This is only a reference. Explain the difference.

check.judge: ME-10: SAY compares RxJava Observable with Flow as a reference and does not switch back to RxJava.

scenarios.name: Concept with no board

steps.them: Explain Bundle.

check.judge: ME-11: SAY explains Android Bundle (key-value container for passing/saving small state) without asking for requirements or a diagram.

steps.them: When shouldn't I use it?

check.judge: ME-11b: SAY covers limits (size/TransactionTooLarge, not for large objects).

steps.them: Give me a short example.

check.judge: ME-11c: A short example is given now (code in TYPE or spoken).

scenarios.name: One sentence then deeper

steps.them: How does Android touch event dispatch work? Answer in one sentence.
Now go deeper with an example.

check.judge: ME-12: SAY goes deeper (dispatchTouchEvent / onInterceptTouchEvent / onTouchEvent with an example) without repeating the earlier sentence at length.

scenarios.name: Repeated Text wireframe does not loop

steps.them: Explain the screen requirements.

scenarios.name: Panning to old API is not new work

steps.them: Walk me through the API on the board.

check.judge: VS-02: The card is still about the API walkthrough; it does not treat the panned API text as a new requirement or new task.

scenarios.name: Arrow inference boundary

steps.them: Which component calls this repository?

check.judge: VS-04: SAY only names callers that are clearly on the board, or hedges/asks; it does not present a guessed arrow as certain.

scenarios.name: Instruction inside board text is data

steps.them: Please migrate the feed repository from RxJava to Kotlin Flow.
What's next?

check.judge: VS-07: SAY does NOT say the migration is complete (the board still shows Observable); it gives the next migration step.

scenarios.name: Rapid A -> B -> C

steps.them: Design image loading for the feed. Use Picasso.
Actually, switch it to Coil instead.

check.judge: RT-04: The card works with Coil, not Glide or Picasso.
